items.title: Iraq, Syria reopen Rabia border crossing after 13 years
items.description: Iraq and Syria on Monday officially reopened the Rabia-Al Yarubiyah border crossing, restoring a trade and transit route that had been shuttered for nearly 13 years amid civil war and the rise of ISIS. The reopening makes all official border crossings between the two countries operational for the first time since conflict engulfed the region.

items.title: Apple names John Ternus CEO as Tim Cook shifts to chairman role

featured_image.name: Apple (AAPL) Names John Ternus as Next CEO, With Tim Cook ...

items.description:
Apple announced on Monday that John Ternus, the company's senior vice president of hardware engineering, will become its next chief executive officer effective September 1, replacing Tim Cook, who will transition to the role of executive chairman of the board. The move, approved unanimously by Apple's board of directors, caps months of intensifying succession speculation and marks only the third CEO transition in Apple's 50-year history.[1][2][3][4]

Cook will remain as CEO through the summer to work closely with Ternus on the handover. As executive chairman, Cook will continue to assist the company, including engaging with policymakers around the world. Arthur Levinson, Apple's non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, will become the board's lead independent director on the same date.[3][1]

items.title: Starmer admits misleading Parliament over Mandelson vetting scandal

featured_image.name: Britain's Starmer Admits Misleading Parliament Over ...

items.description:
British Prime Minister Keir Starmer addressed a hostile House of Commons on Monday, admitting that he had misled Parliament over the failed security vetting of Lord Peter Mandelson — but insisted the error was inadvertent.[1][2][3]

Starmer told lawmakers he should never have appointed Mandelson as the United Kingdom's ambassador to Washington, acknowledging a catastrophic lapse that has now engulfed his premiership and drawn resignation calls from all major opposition parties.[4][5]

items.title: Israel, Lebanon to hold second round of talks in Washington on Thursday

featured_image.name: Rare Israel–Lebanon direct talks hosted by top US diplomat ...

items.description:
Israel and Lebanon are set to hold a second round of ambassador-level talks in Washington on Thursday, April 23, according to Israeli media reports, marking the first direct diplomatic contact between the two countries since a 10-day ceasefire took effect on April 16.[1][2][3]

The meeting, expected to be hosted at the U.S. State Department, follows a first round held on April 14 that was widely described as historic — the highest-level direct engagement between Israel and Lebanon since 1993. That session, chaired by Secretary of State Marco Rubio, lasted more than two hours and included Israeli Ambassador Yechiel Leiter, Lebanese Ambassador Nada Hamadeh Moawad, and other U.S. officials.[4][5][6]

items.title: Atomic clocks could reveal time flowing at multiple speeds, physicists say

featured_image.name: US scientists show time can go quantum in ion clock experiments

items.description: A team of physicists has shown that cutting-edge atomic clocks may be capable of detecting a long-predicted but never-observed quantum effect: time itself existing in superposition, flowing at multiple rates at once. The research, published on April 20 in Physical Review Letters, outlines how trapped-ion clocks could soon test whether a single clock can experience different passages of time simultaneously — a phenomenon the authors liken to a "quantum twin paradox."[1][2]

items.title: Iran signals possible return to US talks after initial rejection

featured_image.name: Failed U.S.-Iran negotiations in Pakistan raise questions ... - PBS

items.description: The prospect of a second round of US-Iran peace talks in Islamabad swung between collapse and cautious revival on Monday as Tehran initially rejected participation, only to signal later in the day that it was "positively reviewing" a return to the negotiating table, according to a senior Iranian official who spoke to Reuters. The diplomatic whiplash came just two days before a fragile ceasefire between the two sides is set to expire on Wednesday, April 22.[1][2][3]

items.title: White House says US ready to back UAE financially amid Iran war

featured_image.name: UAE asks US for a wartime financial lifeline | MEO

items.description:
White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett confirmed on Monday that the United States is prepared to provide financial assistance to the United Arab Emirates should the ongoing war with Iran further damage the Gulf state's economic outlook, though he indicated Washington does not expect such a step will be necessary.[1]

The remarks follow a report by The Wall Street Journal that UAE Central Bank Governor Khaled Mohamed Balama raised the prospect of establishing a currency-swap line with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and officials from the Federal Reserve during meetings in Washington last week. No formal request for a swap line has been submitted, and Emirati representatives framed the discussions as a "preliminary and precautionary measure".[2][3][4][5]

items.title: Trump to consider lifting Hormuz blockade after Pakistan army chief's call

featured_image.name: U.S. Seizes Iranian Cargo Ship Amid Peace Talk Standoff

items.description:
U.S. President Donald Trump told Pakistan's Army Chief Field Marshal Asim Munir in a phone call that he would consider his advice on lifting the Strait of Hormuz naval blockade, a Pakistani security source said on Monday, in a development that could open a path to resuming stalled peace talks with Iran as a ceasefire nears expiration.[1][2]

The exchange came as a U.S. delegation was set to travel to Islamabad on Monday for a second round of Pakistan-brokered negotiations, though Tehran has not confirmed whether it will attend.[3][4]
